# Command reference

<!-- Generated by `delphi docs cli` from the command table in crates/delphi/src/main.rs. Do not edit by hand: change the table and regenerate. -->

`delphi` with no command sets up whatever is missing and opens the console. Options that name a place work on every command that touches a workspace: `--home <dir>` (default `$DELPHI_HOME`, else `~/.delphi`) and `--workspace <name>`. `delphi help <command>` and `delphi <command> --help` print the same text as this page and never create a workspace.

## Start

### `delphi`

Set up whatever is missing, then open the console.

```
  delphi [--no-onboard] [--plain] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

### `delphi chat`

The console, on today's mission or one you name.

```
  delphi chat [--plain] [--inline] [--no-mouse] [--workspace <name>] [--mission <id>] [--home <dir>]
```

`delphi missions` lists the missions you can reopen.

### `delphi run`

One task without a terminal, then a summary.

```
  delphi run "<task>" [--on-card deny|policy:<file>] [--permissions <mode>] [--budget <usd>] [--timeout <dur>]
    [--json|--jsonl] [--mission <id>] [--keep-daemon] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 gates failed · 2 a card was denied · 3 budget · 4 infrastructure ·
5 an optimistic build awaits decision review.

## Set up

### `delphi setup`

Find the model tools you have and connect them.

```
  delphi setup [--yes] [--check] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

### `delphi init`

Create a workspace for a project.

```
  delphi init [--non-interactive] [--workspace <name>] [--project <path>]... [--theme <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

### `delphi project`

Register, scaffold, and inspect directory project scopes.

```
  delphi project register [path] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi project init [path] [--yes] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi project list | scope [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi project index [path] [--refresh] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi project relink <project-id> <new-path> [--home <dir>]
  delphi project clone [path] [--home <dir>]
```

A project is a directory scope; Git is optional. `register` writes the identity marker and central project record. `init` lists paths first, asks for confirmation, and creates only missing project folders and `_index.md`; in non-interactive use, pass `--yes`. Existing files are preserved. `index` reports whether `_index.md` is current; `index --refresh` regenerates it (and `.delphi-index/` category indexes for large projects) from the files allowed by `.gitignore`, `.delphiignore` and the default exclusions (credentials, hidden files, caches, build and dependency trees, files over 2 MiB; symlinks are not followed). A hand-edited `_index.md` is never overwritten: a proposed replacement goes to `.delphi-index/proposed-index.md` and the command exits 3.

### `delphi auth`

Sign in to, or out of, a model endpoint.

```
  delphi auth login <name> [--manual] | status | logout <name> [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

### `delphi endpoints`

Check that each model endpoint answers.

```
  delphi endpoints test [<endpoint id>] [--probe] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

### `delphi connectors`

The connectors that are configured, logged in and pinned.

```
  delphi connectors status | test <name> | pin <name> [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

### `delphi relay`

Send approval cards to your email or Telegram.

```
  delphi relay [check|totp-enroll|totp-check <code>] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

Takes your replies too. Run it in a terminal or a tmux pane.

### `delphi skills`

Agentskills.io skills in and out.

```
  delphi skills check <dir> | export <name> [--out <dir>] | import <dir> --agents <role,role>
    [--description "…"] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

An import is a pending proposal until you /ratify it.

### `delphi bundle`

Check an org bundle: knowledge, skills and behavior to share.

```
  delphi bundle init <dir> --org <org> --name <name>
  delphi bundle validate <dir> [--claude] [--against <previous dir>] [--package] [--report <file>] [--workspace <name>]
  delphi bundle distill [<path|missions/id>...] [--workspace <name>]
  delphi bundle import <plugin dir> [-o <new dir>] [--as <name>] [--org <org>] [--agents <role,role>] [--agent-role <agent>=<role>]
  delphi bundle export <name> --claude-plugin <new dir> [--strip-delphi] | --agents-md [<file>] [--workspace <name>]
  delphi bundle export <name>... --marketplace <dir> --repo <owner/repo|url> --sha <commit> [--ref R] [--subdir D]
  delphi bundle manifest <dir> [--claude]
  delphi bundle sign <dir> [--against <previous dir>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi bundle package <dir> [-o <file.xbundle>] [--vectors]
  delphi bundle add <dir or file.xbundle> | --from-marketplace <repo> <name> [--order N] [--replace-publisher] [--no-vectors] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--trust ratified] [--trust-source] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi bundle add <record id> --from-xenia <org>/<store> [--order N] [--replace-publisher] [--no-vectors] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi bundle store <org>/<store> [--auto-update] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi bundle publish <dir> --to <org>/<store> --url <https git url> --pin <git-tree|git-commit>:<sha> [--subdir D] [--id <record>] [--tags a,b] [--review-by YYYY-MM-DD] [--no-verify-tree] [--home <dir>]
  delphi bundle sources add <dir> <source-id>... [--replace] [--home <dir>]   (copy library sources into the bundle's sources/, with their licence record)
  delphi bundle trust <bundle> --level user_ratified|default [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi bundle trust-source <bundle|origin> [--level user_ratified|default] [--revoke] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi bundle list | remove <name> | update [name] | rollback <name> [--to <hash>] | gc [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi bundle serve [--bundle <org/name>]... [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

init writes a skeleton that validates at once. validate reads the directory and changes nothing; --report writes the redaction report (every
secret, path, address and name the scan found, masked) to a file outside the bundle. distill has the writer role draft knowledge from
allow-listed sources (team context and specs, mission decisions and Council verdicts) into a staging directory of the mission; it writes
nothing into a bundle. package --vectors embeds the knowledge with the installed model into vectors/. manifest writes .delphi-bundle/files.json (and with --claude
.claude-plugin/plugin.json) and prints the bundle hash. sign (a terminal only) signs the manifest with this install's xenia key; package writes a reproducible .xbundle archive. A bundle may carry sources under sources/: bundle.toml `distribution` (`internal` by default, or `public`) says where it is meant to go, a source licence only warns (source-licence, source-attribution, source-sharealike; only `private: true` refuses), and packaging a `public` bundle that carries sources asks you once, in a terminal, to type `publish` after showing each source id and its licence class; the answer is recorded in .delphi-bundle/report.json (licence_acknowledged). An org that adds a bundle vouches for its sources: they are shown `validated · vouched by <org>` only while that bundle entry is in the lock, as data and never instructions.
Every bundle document is a validated bundle source: agents and the Council may cite it, with its bundle and provenance level; it stays data, never instructions, and grants no permission. trust raises ONE bundle's knowledge to user_ratified for its current hash and publisher (`add --trust ratified` does it at install): it needs a terminal and you typing the bundle name (no --yes, no environment switch), and it resets when an update changes the hash or publisher, on rollback and on remove; --level default lowers it at any time. trust-source (`add --trust-source`) deems a source trusted: the same origin AND publisher key (or a roster successor of it), so later updates keep the tier you chose without a prompt while every check still runs; it needs the same typed confirmation (the origin), and --revoke ends it. A bundle can set neither.
add takes a directory or an archive, verifies any signature, prints what it brings, copies it into the cache and makes its
knowledge searchable (`delphi kb search --bundle org/name`); a new publisher key needs --replace-publisher. update re-adds from
the recorded source under that rule and prints the changelog; rollback re-points at an earlier cached version; gc prunes the
cache. serve is a read-only MCP server on stdio for the added bundles' knowledge (resources, and the tools search and get_doc); it writes nothing, opens no port and runs nothing. No model is called to add. Vectors it ships are used only if they match this install's embedder and pass a local spot check
(--no-vectors skips them); the rest are embedded in the background, and `list` shows how far along they are.
import turns a Claude Code plugin into a new bundle directory (it never adds it, and never imports hooks/ or bin/); export writes an added
bundle as a plugin (--claude-plugin), an AGENTS.md fragment, or a marketplace.json; add --from-marketplace fetches the entry's pinned commit.
A bundle can also travel through a xenia store (the org's shared, signed, git-hosted store you joined with `delphi xenia`). `publish` writes a `bundle` record from the signed bundle's own manifest, pointing at the git tree you name, and asks you once, showing the exact bytes. `add --from-xenia` verifies the store, fetches that tree under the same limits as a marketplace add, requires it to hash to the record and to be signed by the member who published it, and records the store's standing: `endorsed` (a steward of another person endorsed these exact bytes, under a current freshness statement) or `member-signed`. `update` follows the record's newer revisions, forward only. `store` lists the store's bundles; with --auto-update it also keeps the levels in the lock current and applies the updates that cannot lower the level or change the publisher.
sources add copies sources from your library into <dir>/sources/ (and turns the section on in bundle.toml). It writes meta.json from the library record (citation fields and the licence record, `internal` when there is none; no status, origin, reliance count or note), source.md when the capture is whole, the excerpts without your purpose notes, and recognised assets. Licence is information, not a gate: nothing is refused for it. The one refusal is a source you flagged private, which never travels in a bundle; the command is also refused inside an agent seat. It refreshes files.json when the bundle has one (sign again if it was signed) and lists the source-licence, source-attribution and source-sharealike warnings `validate` would report. For a public bundle, `package` and `publish` print the sources that carry a licence note and ask you to confirm in a terminal (no --yes); for an internal bundle `publish` asks. The acknowledged ids are written to .delphi-bundle/report.json.
Exit codes: 0 pass · 1 failed · 2 usage.

### `delphi hooks`

Run your observe hooks on events.

```
  delphi hooks [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

Run it in a terminal or a tmux pane. The hooks are in the ratified [hooks] config.

## Work

### `delphi decisions`

Review an optimistic build's provisional decisions.

```
  delphi decisions [list|show <id>|ratify <id…|all-routine>|reject <id> [why]] [--mission <id>]
    [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

This is the text form for a shell. In the console, `/decisions` with no argument opens the decisions pane:
every approval card, provisional decision and agent-raised decision you owe, one at a time.

### `delphi timers`

The wakes the daemon is keeping for roles.

```
  delphi timers [list | set <role> (--in <5m> | --at <time>) [--every <5m>] <note…> | cancel <id>]
    [--mission <id>] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

### `delphi validation`

Score the labelled set; audit, report on and retract validated facts.

```
  delphi validation score [--set <file>] [--results <file>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi validation audit [--card <id>] [--workspace <name>]
  delphi validation report [--workspace <name>]
  delphi validation latch raise --to advisory|ratify --reason "<text>" [--force] [--workspace <name>]
  delphi validation retract --all [--workspace <name>]
  delphi validation unquarantine <fact-id> --reason "<text>" [--workspace <name>]
  delphi validation more <mission> --reason "<text>" [--workspace <name>]
  delphi validation queue [--workspace <name>]
```

Operator-run; every subcommand refuses inside an agent seat, and `audit` needs a terminal. `score` reads the private set (default <home>/operator/validation/claims.json) and prints counts and rates only: claims scored, false-ratified, poisoned passes, wrongly-escalated rate, the rule-of-three bound and the claims new since the last scored run; it also keeps those counts for `report`. `audit` is the blind audit: it shows one claim from the validator's checks and nothing else, asks true, false or unsure, records your answer, and only then shows the sources and the verdict. A fact you call false trips the latch to advisory, withdraws PROMOTE and quarantines the facts of that batch; a would-ratify card left unanswered for seven days quarantines its fact. `report` prints the audit counts, the rule-of-three bound, the origin shares and the token use, then PROMOTE: yes or no with the conditions it missed, and writes promote.json; it never runs the validator. `latch raise` (or the console card, which asks you to type the word) is the only way up from a tripped latch: it needs a reason, starts a new audit batch, and for ratify needs PROMOTE: yes or --force, which is logged as forced. `retract --all` marks every validated fact superseded by its retraction (nothing is deleted; disproved facts are left as they are) and lists the missions recorded as having read one; it does not mark them stale. `unquarantine` returns one quarantined fact to the status it had (or contested), needs a reason and is journaled as yours; it cannot undo a fact you called false in an audit, and while a false audit holds the latch tripped it refuses until `latch raise`. At a mission's 15% share claims are kept as not validated and queued; `queue` lists them, most-referenced first, and `more` raises that mission's cap once (logged, yours alone). Format: docs/reference/validation-set.md.

### `delphi claims`

The library's claims: statements anchored in sources, pulled by pointer.

```
  delphi claims add <text> [--kind fact|episode|procedure|attributed] [--scope personal|project|team|org] [--project <name>]
    [--valid-until YYYY-MM-DD] [--supersedes <claim>] [--origin <page>] [--source <id> --locator <where> --quote <passage>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi claims anchor <claim> --source <id> --quote <passage> [--locator <where>] [--prefix <t>] [--suffix <t>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi claims list [--json] [--home <dir>]
  delphi claims show <claim> [--json] [--home <dir>]
  delphi claims validate <claim> [--home <dir>]
  delphi claims confirm <claim> [--home <dir>]
  delphi claims review [--json] [--home <dir>]
  delphi claims pull <words...> [--project <name>] [--json] [--home <dir>]
```

A claim is a short statement kept once per install in <home>/library/claims/, with anchors into the library's sources: the source, version, locator, the exact quote and a little text on each side. Its status is derived by the daemon and never typed: a new claim reads not validated, and only `validate` (you, in a terminal; refused inside an agent seat) records a validation, which counts only while an anchor still holds. An attributed claim (an opinion) is never validated as a fact. A source held whole is anchored by quote in its text; one that is not (excerpts, pointer) only inside an excerpt you kept, so a claim cannot quote more of a restricted work than the excerpt bounds allow. When a source gets a new version each anchor is looked up again by its quote, then by its surroundings: found moves to the new version, not found marks the claim contested and leaves the old anchor readable under versions/; nothing is re-pointed to different text. A source marked retired contests the claims it alone supports; `sources purge` turns every anchor into it pointer-only (the quote goes with the capture, the citation and quote hash stay) and a claim no other source supports then reads not validated. `sources show` lists how many of a source's claims stood, were contested or disproved. Every mission start pulls claims from this one library by pointer, chosen by the words of the prompt and the project, ranked by status, recency and how often they were relied on; disproved and retired claims are not offered, and a project-scoped claim goes only to its project. The agent gets the id, status label, origin and score, never the text; opening it is a tainted, read-only read, and a claim that rests on a private source is withheld. `pull` shows what a mission start would be handed and records nothing. The library records which missions were handed a claim (`cited_by`). `review` lists claims that may disagree (two live claims of one kind that say nearly the same thing in different words; a word-overlap match with no model, so it may be a false alarm, and neither is picked) and claims due for review (not confirmed for 90 days, or `--valid-until` within 14 days); both are read on demand and the daemon changes nothing. `confirm` says a claim still holds: it moves only the date and cannot raise a status. The same items appear in the daily digest. `add`, `anchor`, `validate` and `confirm` are refused inside an agent seat.

### `delphi pages`

A readable page generated from the library's claims, and dispute from it.

```
  delphi pages show <topic words...> [--draft <file>] [--style apa|mla|chicago|plain] [--home <dir>]
  delphi pages check <file> [--home <dir>]
  delphi pages dispute <claim> --note <what is wrong> [--home <dir>]
  delphi pages search <question words...> [--internal | --external] [--json] [--home <dir>]
  delphi pages expand <question words...> [--json] [--home <dir>]
  delphi pages list [--json] [--home <dir>]
  delphi pages pin|unpin <key> [--home <dir>]
```

A page is generated, never a source, never edited and never trusted text (spec 057). The daemon writes the banner on top ("Generated page. Not authoritative. ...") and, at the bottom, a bibliography and citations table with one row per cited source or claim (or "no sources cited", marked unsupported in the banner). The body cites with [s-source-id] and [c-claim-id] markers after the sentences or paragraph they support; the glyphs ● validated, ○ not validated, ◆ contested, ✕ disproved are derived by the daemon. Without --draft the body is the library's claims, the unvalidated ones under a visible "Noted, not validated" heading. With --draft a file of body text someone proposed (a model, say), the daemon runs the mechanical check and rejects the page, listing each finding, exit 1, if a marker names a missing, retired, purged, disproved or (on an external page) private record or misstates its status; a quotation is not verbatim in a cited source's stored text (checked against the recorded hash) or a quote block cites no source; a table has no citation; an image is not an asset of a cited library source (written lib: then the source id, a slash and the file name); a link is in no cited source's record; or the text carries its own banner or table. Numbers, dates and proper names found in no cited material are not rejected but reported as unverified figures. `check` runs the same check on a whole page file (banner, body, table) and prints the findings. Pages are cached by a hash of the claims they were built from, so a changed or disputed claim rebuilds them. A claim resting on a private source is left off. `dispute` is your "this is wrong" on a sentence: it files a contested mark with your note on the cited claim, which then reads not validated until the contest is resolved, and is refused inside an agent seat. `search` finds what the library holds for the words and has the writer role compose a page from it, which the daemon then checks mechanically and the validator checks sentence by sentence; a page that fails twice is shown as the claims alone (exit 1). --internal never touches the web; --external also searches the engines in [search] and captures a few results as noted, not validated, sources (a query that names a private source is not sent, and a private source never reaches an external page). Without either, [library.pages] external decides (ask means internal unless you say --external). Pages are cached by the material's hashes: a changed source, an expired external page ([library.pages] external_ttl) or a new matching record marks the page stale and it is rebuilt on the next search; `pin` keeps a page out of eviction. A page costs a writer call and a validator call, counted against the validator's share of the week (spec 040 §20) and [library.pages] per_day; a cached page costs nothing. Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 rejected, failed or claims only · 2 usage · 4 infrastructure.

### `delphi sources`

The library's sources: capture, excerpts, bibliography.

```
  delphi sources add <url | file | doi> [--level full|excerpts|pointer] [--licence <id>] [--private]
    [--title <t>] [--rights-holder <name>] [--attribution <text>] [--max-text-mib <n>] [--max-source-mib <n>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi sources list [--json] [--home <dir>]
  delphi sources show <id> [--json] [--offline] [--home <dir>]
  delphi sources history <id> [--json] [--home <dir>]
  delphi sources excerpt add <id> --locator <where> --purpose <why> (--text <passage> | --file <file>) [--prefix <t>] [--suffix <t>]
    [--work-bytes <n>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi sources excerpt list <id> [--json] [--home <dir>]
  delphi sources bib [<id>...] [--format apa|mla|chicago|plain|csl-json|bibtex] [--home <dir>]
  delphi sources purge <id> [--home <dir>]
  delphi sources acquire status|run|batch [<batch>]|accept <batch> [<id>...]|skip <batch> [<id>...] [--home <dir>]
  delphi sources acquire rule add --topic <t>... --archive <id>... [--max-mib <n>] | list | remove <rule> [--home <dir>]
  delphi sources reading-list list|show <list> | add <list> <id>... [--title <t>] | remove <list> <id> [--home <dir>]
```

One library per install, in <home>/library/. A URL is fetched by the validation fetcher (https only, no private addresses, size cap, cloaking check). The licence decides the level: open licences and your own material are kept whole, restricted ones as excerpts, an unknown one as a pointer; --private keeps a restricted source whole for your own use and it never leaves this install. Everything captured reads not validated. Limits: 64 MiB of text and 512 MiB per source, 20 GiB for the library; over a limit the capture falls back and says so. `purge` deletes the capture and keeps the citation and the content hash. Metadata is read by code, never guessed: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA, the revision from the ETag), a DOI's landing page (citation meta tags) and a Gutenberg header; a field the page does not state is left empty. `show` is an open: if the source was last checked more than 30 days ago it is fetched once through the same fetcher (no tokens; skipped offline or with --offline), an unchanged page only moves last_checked, a changed one becomes a new version with a change note and the old one kept, and a gone one (404/410) is marked retired. `excerpt add` keeps one quoted passage with its locator and purpose: at most 4 KiB each, and for a restricted source not held whole at most 10% of the work or 16 KiB in total (the work's length is recorded at capture, or give --work-bytes); each excerpt carries an anchor (quote, prefix and suffix, and a character range when the text is held) that is looked up again when the source changes, and one that cannot be found is marked contested, never re-pointed. `bib` writes a bibliography from the citation fields alone, in apa, mla, chicago or plain text, or as csl-json or bibtex for a reference manager; private sources are left out of every export. `history` lists every kept capture, oldest first, with its change note (sizes and the sections that came or went, no model) and how many claim anchors point at it; a purge deletes the earlier ones. `add`, `purge`, `excerpt add` and `bib` are refused inside an agent seat.
Acquisition (off until `[library.acquire] enabled = true`): once a day the daemon looks for public-domain and research sources matching your projects and `interests` in the archives listed in context/sources/archives.toml (and operator/archives.toml), and puts what it found in the digest as ONE batch, never a blocking prompt; nothing is fetched until you accept. `accept` captures the chosen items in full under the archive's own terms (the archive's rate limits, its notice and attribution kept, the public-domain basis recorded from the archive's own record, never typed by an agent); `skip` declines them for good. A standing rule (`acquire rule add`) takes anything on those topics from those archives up to a size without asking. The byte budget (`byte_budget_mib`) stops acquisition and deletes nothing; acquired sources read not validated and their claims start noted. `run` searches now without the scout's model call. A private source's tags never leave the install. `reading-list` keeps named lists of source ids. All of it is refused inside an agent seat.

### `delphi route`

Which bundle agent fits a task (a dry run).

```
  delphi route "<task>" [--domain <d>] [--role <role>] [--limit <1-5>] [--json] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
  delphi route --eval <labeled.json> [--json] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

Ranks the agents of the added bundles for a task the way the orchestrator's `search_agent_registry` tool does: by name, tags,
domain and summary, plus the local embedding model when one is installed. Nothing is dispatched, no model is called and nothing
is created. `--eval` takes a JSON list of {"task", "target"} (target is `bundle:<bundle>/<agent>`) and prints recall at 1, 3 and 5,
latency and the tokens of the domain index against the uncapped flat list. Turn routing on with `[routing] registry = "auto"`.

### `delphi needs`

What the roadmap is waiting on evidence for.

```
  delphi needs [add <item> <why>] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

After the roadmap items it prints the fact validator's open work, once it has run here: the blind-audit
cards waiting (and the oldest's age) and the PROMOTE line from the last `delphi validation report`.
It reads files only and never runs the validator.

### `delphi kb`

The knowledge base: index it, search it.

```
  delphi kb index | reindex | stats | search <query> [--role <role>] [--untrusted] [--staged]
  delphi kb serve [--bind <host:port>] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

### `delphi observe`

The read-only live window (also: delphi narrator).

```
  delphi observe [dashboard|council|epic|agents|timeline|changes]
    [--once] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

--once prints one frame as text; it works without a terminal.

## Inspect

### `delphi status`

Workspace, daemon, models, health and mission at a glance.

```
  delphi status [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

Needs no terminal. Exits 1 only if `delphi doctor` finds a failure.

### `delphi missions`

The workspace's missions, newest first.

```
  delphi missions [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

Reopen one with `delphi chat --mission <id>`.

### `delphi changelog`

What the team recorded as finished, for a pull request.

```
  delphi changelog [--mission <id>] [--session <s_0001>] [--since <date or time>] [--json]
    [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

Prints Markdown by session, from the mission's log (the latest unless --mission). --json: one line per change.

### `delphi release`

Whether this build is a signed release.

```
  delphi release [status]
```

Signed by the maintainers' key, unsigned (a local or development build), or invalid. Needs no terminal.

### `delphi sessions`

The finished console sessions, to review later.

```
  delphi sessions [--mission <id>] [--limit <n>] [--full] [--json] [--home <dir>]
```

Written when a session ends (/new, or a daemon restart): the first words of what was asked, the changes recorded, and the summary when [session] summary is on. Reads the central log; calls no model.

### `delphi tools`

How tools are used, and how often models record their changes.

```
  delphi tools [--mission <id> | --all] [--json | --prom] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

Per model: runs that changed something and recorded a change. --prom: Prometheus text. Counts only.

## Set up

### `delphi customize`

Teach Delphi a note, a rule, a skill or a profile line yourself.

```
  delphi customize note "<text>" [--mission <id>]
  delphi customize rule "<text>" [--scope workspace|operator] [--why "…"] [--replace <ID> | --remove <ID>]
  delphi customize skill <dir> --agents <role,role> [--description "…"]
  delphi customize profile ["<line>" | --file <path>]
    [--yes] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

What you write is yours: a rule, a skill or a profile line is ratified as you write it, after the same checks a proposal gets (no relaxing a rule, the caps, no near-duplicate). `note` only stages a note for review. Each verb needs a terminal; `--yes` skips the typed yes, not the terminal. A rule applies from the next task.

## Inspect

### `delphi retro`

Rules the Orchestrator proposed, waiting for your review.

```
  delphi retro list [--mission <id>] [--json]
  delphi retro show <mission>/<id> [--json]
  delphi retro stale [--json]
  delphi retro mine [--mission <id>] [--json]
  delphi retro accept <mission>/<id> [--scope workspace|operator]
  delphi retro reject <mission>/<id> [--reason <text>]
  delphi retro promote <project-id> <record>... --summary <text> --mission <id> [--uncertainty <text>]
  delphi retro promotions [--json]
  delphi retro withdraw <entry> [--reason <text>]
    [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

Proposals are made with the Orchestrator's `suggest_rule` tool and are never loaded into a prompt until you ratify them. `accept` and `reject` need a terminal and a typed yes, and `accept` needs the daemon stopped; `--scope` ratifies at a different scope than proposed. A promotion (`promote`) is a proposal to keep a summary of eligible project memory records as home memory: it records the summary, the records, their hashes and the home records it was checked against, and shows any duplicate or conflicting home entry without merging it. Accepting one runs the checks again and refuses if a record became private, retired or secret-bearing or if the proposal or home memory changed since; the entry keeps its provenance and its source tier and validates nothing. `reject` records only the outcome and your reason. `withdraw` retires a promoted entry with an audit reference and deletes nothing. `stale` lists staged notes past their `valid_until` date and rules files not confirmed within 90 days; it changes nothing. `mine` ranks the failed or looping spans of a mission (a loop stop, a red gate, a denied card, an escalation, repeated tool failures) by a cause computed from event kinds and codes, never from text, and writes the report to the mission's `reports/trace-mining.json`; it applies nothing.

### `delphi agent`

Promote or nerf a role: the class of model it is assigned.

```
  delphi agent promote|nerf <role> [--kind <task kind>] [--reason <text>]
  delphi agent grades
    [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

A grade (-2 to 2) is kept in the ratified [grades] table. promote and nerf edit config.toml and show the diff; nothing changes until you /ratify it.
grades lists them with the measured results beside each. Delphi may suggest a grade and never applies one. Refused inside an agent seat.

### `delphi learn`

Notes staged from denials, corrections, retries and escalations.

```
  delphi learn list [--mission <id>] [--json]
  delphi learn show <mission>/<id> [--json]
  delphi learn drop <mission>/<id>
    [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

Staged notes are never loaded into a prompt; they wait for review. `drop` needs the daemon stopped. Capture is set in [learning] in config.toml.

### `delphi capabilities`

What each model CLI here can use: connectors, skills, models.

```
  delphi capabilities [--refresh] [--ask] [--json] [--quiet] [--models] [--project <dir>]... [--home <dir>]
```

--models lists every discovered model with its class (spec 056; takes --workspace); one no longer
listed is kept as gone.
Asks each CLI's own list commands and reads the skill directories; saves <home>/capabilities.json.
Setup and update refresh it in the background. --ask also asks the claude and agy models what they can
use; that answer is shown apart and is not verified. Calls no model otherwise.

### `delphi logs`

The error log: what went wrong, with context.

```
  delphi logs [--lines <n>] [--since 1h] [--level error|warn|debug] [--component <name>] [--mission <id>] [--json] [--follow] [--path] [--home <dir>]
```

Reads $DELPHI_HOME/logs/delphi.log.jsonl, written by the CLI, the daemon and the console: errors and panics by default, redacted, 10 MB x 3 files.
DELPHI_LOG=off|error|warn|debug or [logging] level in <home>/operator/config.toml sets what is kept. Read-only and offline. --path prints the file's location.
Components: cli, daemon, engine, harness, provider, ui, xenia, relay, tool.

### `delphi debug`

Pack a redacted slice of the log for sharing.

```
  delphi debug bundle [--since 24h] [-o <file>] [--mission <id>] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

Writes one .tar.gz (mode 0600, never over an existing file): the log slice, the `delphi doctor` report, version and OS, the config's key paths with values
redacted, and the last events of the mission (types and short status fields only; no prompts, outputs or file contents). Prints what it included. Read-only and offline.

### `delphi doctor`

Check the workspace, its files and its models.

```
  delphi doctor [--fix] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>] [--require-providers]
```

--fix asks before each repair and needs a terminal.

### `delphi models`

The model pool: usable, out of quota, cooling down.

```
  delphi models [--probe] [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

### `delphi daemon`

The background process: status, stop, restart.

```
  delphi daemon status|stop|restart [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

### `delphi lint`

Check a repository's Delphi files.

```
  delphi lint --repo <path>
```

### `delphi check`

The deterministic checks behind the built-in skills.

```
  delphi check <dag|handoff|provenance|rules|review-md|spec|kb|tui|skill> <path> [--repo <path>]
  delphi check fact <claim.json> [--home <dir>]
  delphi check record <mission-dir> --event <seq> [--hash <h>]
```

`record` verifies one event in a mission log: its hash chain against the daemon's stored head (no model,
no network). An agent-authored event only warns "an agent wrote this". `fact` reads {claim, needed_for, kind,
snapshots: [ids]} and checks the claim against snapshots the daemon stored: origins, independence, classes.
It makes no network call and runs no model; the judge and the contradiction search are the daemon's.

## Maintain

### `delphi update`

The program, the built-in files, then the daemons.

```
  delphi update [--check] [--version vX.Y.Z | --dev] [--rollback] [--review] [--no-restart] [--allow-downgrade]
    [--workspace <name>] [--home <dir>]
```

--dev installs the latest build of main. --rollback undoes all three steps. --review leaves the release's
changes pending for /ratify instead of ratifying them.

### `delphi train`

Training mode: check, price and run cases that test Delphi itself.

```
  delphi train validate [--suite <name>] [--repo <path>]
  delphi train plan --budget-usd <n> [--suite <name>] [--split dev|holdout|all] [--seeds <n>] [--home <new dir>] [--repo <path>]
  delphi train run --budget-usd <n> --template-home <dir> --work-dir <new dir> [--overlay <dir> | --arms-file <f>] [--case <id>] [--seeds <n>] [--resume] [--pace-window <0-1>] [--allow-sleep] [--dry-run]
```

For a source checkout (it needs dev/train/suites). validate reads every case and names what is wrong; plan lists the cases a run
would use and the most it could cost, and refuses a budget below that. Neither runs anything or calls a model.
run SPENDS MONEY: each case runs `delphi run` in a copy of the template home, baseline and (with --overlay) candidate, and prints pass rates.
Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 problems · 2 usage · 3 over budget.

### `delphi xenia`

The org's shared, signed memory store: join, sync, status, publish, endorse.

```
  delphi xenia whoami | help [topic] | explain <slug or message>   [--json]
  delphi xenia join <url> --org <o> --store <s> --admin <fingerprint> --head <epoch>:<hash> [--allow-local]
  delphi xenia sync [--auto-update-bundles] | status [--store <org>/<store>] [--json]
  delphi xenia publish <file> --title <t> --summary <s> --promoted [--tags a,b] [--review-by <date>]
  delphi xenia publish --bundle <dir> --url <https url> --pin <git-tree|git-commit>:<sha> [--id <record>]
  delphi xenia endorse|dispute|retract|withdraw|restore <id> [--scope a,b] [--note <n>] [--reason <r>]
  delphi xenia republish --old <did> | admin add|remove|rotate|show|sign|publish|refresh|genesis ...
```

Commands that sign show the exact bytes and want the card's code typed at a terminal. Start: `delphi xenia help`.

### `delphi docs`

Print the command reference or a man page.

```
  delphi docs cli | man | catalog [--repo <dir>] | coverage
```

Generated from the table behind --help, so it is never out of date. `cli` is Markdown (it is docs/reference/cli.md); `man` is roff; `catalog` lists the built-in roles and skills from their manifests (docs/reference/catalog.md), read from a checkout. `coverage` is Markdown (docs/reference/harness-coverage.md): the disposition of every flag and command of the claude, agy and codex CLIs, from the manifests Delphi checks against each CLI's --help (specs/046).

### `delphi completions`

Print a shell completion script.

```
  delphi completions bash|zsh|fish
```

For example: `delphi completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_delphi`.

### `delphi help`

This list, or one command's options.

```
  delphi help [<command>]
```

`delphi <command> --help` says the same.

## Environment

| Variable | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- |
| `DELPHI_HOME` | where Delphi keeps its files (default ~/.delphi); --home overrides it |
| `DELPHI_WORKSPACE` | the workspace to use when --workspace is not given |
| `DELPHI_UI` | the delphi-ui program to use (default: next to delphi) |
| `DELPHI_THEME` | dark or light, when the terminal cannot say |
| `NO_COLOR` | no colour at all; TERM=dumb also drops styling |
| `DELPHI_REDUCE_MOTION` | 1 stops every console animation (also /reduce-motion) |
| `DELPHI_NO_ONBOARD` | 1 skips the first-run questions |
| `DELPHI_LOG` | off, error (default), warn or debug: what `delphi logs` keeps |

`delphi --version` prints the release of this program.
